newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB expects Swiss Q4 money supply to grow 4.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: SNB expects Swiss Q4 money supply to grow 4.5 pct.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) said demand for bank notes should continue to grow in the fourth quarter and forecast an increase in average seasonally-adjusted central bank money supply to 31.6 billion Swiss francs.
"Central bank money supply should thus surpass the level seen in the fourth quarter of 1995 by 4.5 percent," the SNB said in an advance release of its monthly report for October.
It noted that this growth rate was signficantly more than predicted at the end of 1995. This prediction also takes into account the effect of changes in demand for sight deposits.

The expected growth for bank notes will mainly be driven by the slightly lower interest rate level on money and capital markets, while demand from private consumption will only contribute slightly to the expected rise, the SNB said.
In the third quarter seasonally-adjusted central bank money supply rose by 31.349 billion francs on average, surpassing the forecast from July by more than 200 million francs.
Compared with the fourth quarter of 1995, the increase in the third quarter amounted to 3.6 percent.
On an annualised basis, the rise amounts to 4.9 percent.

Compared with the second quarter, the third quarter increase amounted to 362 million francs, pushing central bank money by some 100 million francs, or by 0.4 percent, above the medium-term target range.
In the second quarter, central bank money had exceeded the target path by 0.5 percent, the SNB said.
This target deviation was already in the second quarter mainly due to the strong expansion in sight deposits.
In the third quarter, sight deposits rose by some 200 million francs from the second quarter and were thus some 3.0 billion francs above the level seen a year ago.
"Monetary policy appears, when measured against the rise in sight deposits and central bank money, to be somewhat more expansive than it is in reality," the SNB said.

In September the average level of sight deposits eased by some 100 million francs to 3.099 billion while notes in circulation on average rose 2.1 percent over the previous month's level with 27.752 billion.
Seasonally adjusted central bank money increased by 3.7 percent to 31.353 billion francs in September from the fourth quarter of 1995. On an annualised level, the increase amounted to 4.4 percent.
As already known, bank demand for sight deposits rose markedly in August due to exceptional influences, SNB said.
Several banks drew down their postal checking accounts and wanted to increase sight deposits by the same amount.

"The additional demand lead to renewed tensions in the money market," the SNB said, adding that the Swiss franc also rose in value during the same period following a significant depreciation in the first half of the year.

These tensions in the money market, as a consequence of the shift in demand for sight deposits, led the SNB to inject signficantly more liquidity into the markets to push money market rates down to previous levels.
On September 26 the SNB also cut the discount rate to 1.00 percent, underscoring that the decline in interest rates should continue for while.

Following the cut in the discount rate, money market rates eased and overnight money fluctuated mainly between 1.25 and 1.5 percent. On average money market rates fell 54 basis points to 1.30 percent.
During September money market rates fluctuated between 1-1/8 and 1-3/4 percent compared with a range of 1-1/2 to 2-3/8 percent during August.
Rates for one to three month deposits eased by around 70 basis points during the third quarter, the SNB added.
-- Peter Nielsen, Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
